subject: Stabilization sprint & staged rollout — canary targets and ramp metrics
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Priya Menon <priya@sablebridge.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stabilization sprint & staged rollout — canary targets and ramp metrics

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for signing; welcome aboard. I wanted to put a short, pragmatic stabilization sprint on your radar: instead of a big-bang cutover, we propose a four-week staged rollout embedded in the MAP that focuses on (1) canary traffic slices, (2) training and enablement for your ops team, and (3) measurable ramp metrics so we can de-risk the first 30 days.

Attached is a first-pass stabilization_map_v1.xlsx and a companion canary_metric_definitions.md. High level:

- Week 0 (pre-cutover): final config lock, access handoffs, test accounts provisioned
- Week 1: 5% canary traffic, daily health checks, SLO telemetry populated; ops runbook dry-run on Thursday
- Week 2: 20% traffic, guided training session (recorded), two small model parameter tweaks allowed as regressions are monitored
- Week 3: 60% traffic, full feature toggle validation, support on-call in place for extended hours
- Week 4: 100% and handback to SableBridge with runbooks and metric baselines

Canary success criteria (short): 
- Latency p95 within agreed threshold across the canary population
- Error rate <0.2% sustained for 48 hours
- No material quality regression against the evaluation prompt set (automated eval pass rate >= 92%)

If that aligns, I’ll post the MAP to the shared Drive and propose a quick Monday 30-min alignment to lock the canary slice and training dates. Questions or immediate conflicts?

Best,
Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0168
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Stabilization sprint & staged rollout — canary targets and ramp metrics

Thanks Markus — this looks sensible and appropriately cautious. A few quick asks from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Can you confirm whether the 5% canary will be scoped by customer segment (we want to ensure higher-risk accounts are excluded) or by random sampling?
2) We need the SOC2-in-scope evidence and the runtime logging retention appendix (Tim, can you follow up on the outbound access questions?)
3) For training, can the session be recorded and include a short ops checklist (2 pages) we can hand to our on-call?

If you can confirm the above, we’re comfortable moving forward with the proposed cadence. Monday 30-min alignment works — slot us 09:30 PT if you can.

-priya

Priya Menon

Quick notes after skimming the MAP and matching to our Templates library:

- Canary scoping: we recommend segment-based canaries. We’ll propose an inclusion list (low-risk accounts) and an exclusion list (enterprise accounts > $250k ARR) — that keeps critical accounts out until week 3. I’ve added the preliminary lists in the spreadsheet (tab: canary-slices).
- SOC2 & retention: attaching the short appendix (data-retention-appendix.pdf) and a pointer to the SOC2 evidence bundle (we’ll deliver through the secure portal; link below).
- Ops checklist & training: will produce a 2-page Ops Checklist and 45-min recorded walkthrough targeting your NOC. Camila will lead the session but Grace will own the follow-up enablement tasks.

I’ve also included an initial set of metric thresholds in canary_metric_definitions.md — note the automated eval harness will run nightly against your evaluation prompt set and surface any regressions to the MAP dashboard.

Next steps: Markus — I’ll publish a Drive MAP with the locked slices and proposed training slots; Priya — confirm 09:30 PT Monday and I’ll send the invite.

Thanks,
Camila

Hi all —

Thanks for the fast turn. We’ve published the collaborative MAP here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1AbCdefGhIjK-stabilization-MAP (link above).

Confirming:
- Canary sampling will be segment-based (Per Camila: inclusion/exclusion lists in the MAP).
- SOC2 evidence portal link will be shared via secure channel by EOD Tuesday (Camila, Grace, please coordinate).
- Training 09:30 PT Monday confirmed; invite sent.

Operationally we’ll treat Week 1 as a reduced hours watch (08:00–20:00 PT support window) and move Week 2 to extended coverage if metrics are stable. We’ll use the automated eval harness and the MAP dashboard to run daily quality checks — any regression alert triggers an immediate rollback to prior model/parameters and a retrospective within 24 hours.

Priya — if you’re good with that, set the MAP to ‘accepted’ in the Drive and we’ll treat the training and canary slices as committed actions.

Markus
